heroDescription: From the Boston Patriots' AFL beginnings to Foxborough and six Super Bowl-winning seasons, explore the people, places and turning points behind New England's football history.
timelineKicker: AFL roots, Foxborough and championship eras

timeline.title: Boston receives an AFL franchise
timeline.description: Billy Sullivan secured an American Football League franchise on November 22. A naming contest led to the Patriots identity, connecting the new club to New England's history.

timeline.title: The Boston Patriots begin play
timeline.description: The Patriots opened their first regular season with a 13–10 loss to Denver on September 9. Eight days later, a 28–24 victory over the New York Titans gave Boston its first regular-season win.

timeline.title: An Eastern Division breakthrough
timeline.description: The Patriots defeated Buffalo 26–8 in a playoff for the AFL Eastern crown. It was an early postseason breakthrough for coach Mike Holovak's team.

timeline.title: New England becomes the name
timeline.description: The club changed its name from Boston to New England Patriots and moved to a new stadium in Foxborough. The move established a permanent home after the team's early years at several Boston-area venues.

timeline.title: Three road wins lead to Super Bowl XX
timeline.description: Raymond Berry's Patriots went 11–5 and entered the playoffs as a wild card. Three consecutive road playoff wins delivered the franchise's first AFC championship before Chicago won Super Bowl XX on January 26, 1986.

timeline.title: Robert Kraft purchases the team
timeline.description: Kraft acquired the Patriots in 1994, following earlier ownership changes from Billy Sullivan to Victor Kiam and James Orthwein. His purchase began a new chapter for the franchise in New England.

timeline.title: Back to the Super Bowl
timeline.description: The 1996 Patriots reached a second Super Bowl after beating Jacksonville 20–6 in the AFC Championship Game. Green Bay won Super Bowl XXXI 35–21 on January 26, 1997.

timeline.title: A first Lombardi Trophy
timeline.description: The 2001 season ended with a 20–17 victory over the St. Louis Rams on February 3, 2002. Adam Vinatieri's 48-yard field goal as time expired secured New England's first Super Bowl championship.

timeline.title: A new home opens with a championship banner
timeline.description: Gillette Stadium hosted its first Patriots regular-season game on September 9. New England celebrated the previous season's championship and defeated Pittsburgh 30–14 in the new stadium's Monday night opener.

timeline.title: Three titles in four seasons
timeline.description: New England beat Carolina 32–29 in Super Bowl XXXVIII on February 1, 2004, then Philadelphia 24–21 in Super Bowl XXXIX on February 6, 2005. Those wins completed a run of three championships in four football seasons.

timeline.title: A 16–0 regular season
timeline.description: A 38–35 win over the New York Giants on December 29 completed the first 16–0 regular season in NFL history. The Patriots reached Super Bowl XLII, where the Giants won 17–14 on February 3, 2008.

timeline.title: Butler's interception seals a fourth championship
timeline.description: Tom Brady threw four touchdown passes and Malcolm Butler intercepted Seattle at the goal line with 20 seconds left. New England won 28–24 on February 1, 2015, completing its fourth Super Bowl-winning season.

timeline.title: A comeback from 28–3
timeline.description: Trailing Atlanta by 25 points in the third quarter, New England rallied to win 34–28 in overtime on February 5, 2017. James White scored three touchdowns as the Patriots earned their fifth Super Bowl title.

timeline.title: Defense delivers a sixth title
timeline.description: The Patriots defeated the Los Angeles Rams 13–3 on February 3, 2019. Their sixth Super Bowl victory completed the championship stretch shared by head coach Bill Belichick and quarterback Tom Brady.

timeline.title: Tom Brady enters the Patriots Hall of Fame
timeline.description: Brady was inducted into the Patriots Hall of Fame on June 12 in a ceremony at Gillette Stadium. The honor recognized a New England career spanning the 2000–2019 seasons and six Super Bowl championships.

eras.title: Boston's AFL beginnings
eras.description: The Patriots started as an AFL charter member and played as Boston through 1970. The early period brought an Eastern Division championship and a search for a lasting home before the move to Foxborough.

eras.title: Foxborough and the first conference champions
eras.description: The new regional name and home established the setting for the next generations. The 1985 and 1996 teams reached the Super Bowl before New England's championship breakthrough in the following decade.

eras.title: The Belichick–Brady championships
eras.description: Super Bowl wins after the 2001, 2003, 2004, 2014, 2016 and 2018 seasons define the title-winning span. Last-second kicks, a goal-line interception, an overtime comeback and a defensive win gave those championships distinct stories.

eras.title: Remembering the people behind the seasons
eras.description: The Patriots Hall of Fame connects the franchise's eras through players, coaches and contributors. Its honorees include early stars, offensive linemen, defenders and specialists as well as the quarterbacks of the better-known championship years.

methodology: This independent overview uses New England Patriots historical records, the Patriots Hall of Fame and the Pro Football Hall of Fame. Timeline labels follow football seasons where relevant; descriptions give the calendar dates of postseason games. The championship count describes the six winning seasons from 2001 through 2018, not a prediction about later seasons. Player selections span eras and are not a ranking. Timeline entries, eras and figures link to their sources.
